place.title: Place {ref} (passive buzzer module)
place.text: Push the buzzer module {ref}'s 3 pins into column f, one pin per row: GND into hole {hole.gnd}, I/O into {hole.io} and VCC into {hole.vcc}. The buzzer faces up.
place.tip: Read the labels printed next to the pins: GND, I/O, VCC. If yours are in another order, follow the labels, not the picture.

why: {ref} is a passive buzzer: it only sounds while the Pico switches its signal on and off very fast (PWM), and that speed sets the note. This module is on while its I/O pin is LOW, so the program keeps the pin HIGH when it should be quiet.

wire.ground: This connects {ref}'s GND pin to ground.
wire.power: This powers {ref} from 3.3 V, not 5 V: the module is on while I/O is LOW, and from 5 V the Pico's 3.3 V HIGH couldn't switch it off.
wire.out: {pin} drives {ref}: switching it on and off hundreds or thousands of times a second (PWM) makes the tone.
